From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>

Subject: PII handling for prompts/outputs — follow-up & confirmation

Hi Alice —

Great to meet today. Quick recap from our discovery call and the specific answers you asked for on prompts/outputs and PII handling. I’ve attached a short summary (redwood-pii-summary.pdf) that mirrors the points below.

Recap / what we store by default (hosted API):
- Request metadata (timestamps, model, token counts): stored for operational/analytics purposes.
- Full prompt text and model outputs: stored in request/response logs when request logging is enabled (default for hosted).
- System/agent-level logs (errors, routing): retained for debugging.

Retention & logging controls:
- Hosted API default retention: 30 days for request/response logs and traces.
- Retention configurable per-account (0–90 days) for enterprise contracts; Dedicated/Private deployments can be configured to 0 days (no persistent logs) by policy.
- We support a "no_persist" flag customers can set on requests to avoid storing request/response payloads.
- Redaction: Redwood offers server-side redaction pipelines (PII regex masks) and customers can perform client-side redaction before sending.

Data residency & encryption:
- Hosted API: regional endpoints (us / eu) — logs remain in the selected region for hosted accounts.
- Dedicated / Private: customer-managed VPCs and data can be pinned to customer region; supports AWS region residency.
- Encryption at rest using AES-256; customer KMS/HSM integration available for Dedicated/Private.

Model training and usage:
- Outputs and prompts are not used to train Redwood-owned models without explicit opt-in. We can document that in a contract clause if needed.

Next steps / asks for you:
1) Confirm whether FinCo needs: full no-persist on all requests, or specific routes only.
2) Confirm desired retention (0 / 30 / 90 days) for logs.
3) Confirm data residency requirement (US-only / EU / other).
4) Share any legal/security checklist items we should address (I saw Bob on the call — happy to loop him in).

I’ll loop Neha (security) for a final technical confirmation and any evidence we can provide (SOC 2 artifacts, architecture diagrams).

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the questions. Confirming the technical details below so FinCo has a written record for procurement/legal.

What is stored (by default, hosted API):
- Request metadata: timestamps, route IDs, token counts, model identifiers (retained for analytics/ops).
- Prompt text & model outputs: stored in request/response logs only when logging is enabled.

Retention windows (typical):
- Hosted API default: 30 days for request/response logs and traces.
- Hosted retention configurable to any value between 0 and 90 days for enterprise plans via account policy.
- Dedicated / Private: retention is controlled by customer policy; we can set persistent logging to 0 days (no storage) at deployment time.

Logging controls / redaction: 
- No_persist flag: customers can set a per-request header (x-redwood-no-persist: true) which prevents storage of request/response payloads. Metadata and billing counters are still recorded.
- Server-side redaction: optional pipeline component; supports regex-based masking and named-entity PII detectors. Can be deployed for your account to redact before persistence.
- Client-side best practice: perform deterministic redaction or tokenization of highly sensitive fields before sending.

Data residency and encryption:
- Regional hosting: hosted API endpoints are region-scoped (us / eu). Logs for an account are stored in the chosen region.
- Dedicated/Private: customer-managed VPC + storage; data remains in customer-selected region.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest; TLS 1.2+ in transit. Dedicated/Private supports customer KMS (AWS KMS or HSM) with customer-managed keys.

Model training and usage: 
- Redwood does not use customer prompts or outputs to train or improve Redwood-owned models unless the customer provides explicit opt-in. We are happy to include the following sample clause in the MSA: 
  "Customer Data (including prompts and model outputs) will not be used to train, modify, or improve Redwood's models or derivative models without Customer's prior written consent."

Evidence and artifacts we can provide:
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), architecture diagram showing regional boundaries, sample retention policy config screenshots, and a short runbook describing the no_persist header.

Suggested next step: 30-min technical sync with our security/infra team + FinCo infra/security to finalize retention, redaction scope, and contract language. Rishi — can you propose Tue/Wed availability and I’ll bring the SOC2 artifact and retention screenshots to the call.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
